topic: Cloud Wars: Rise of the Data Kings
description: Subtitle: How AWS launched the cloud era in 2006, Azure and Google chased fast, Alibaba conquered APAC — and Oracle got left behind. A dramatic market-shift story (2006–2026) showing one giant's dominance, rivals' meteoric climbs, and a legacy player's collapse.
youtube_description:
From a tiny 2006 service to a multi-hundred-billion-dollar business: this chart race tells the real story of cloud dominance. AWS invented the category and exploded. Microsoft and Google poured billions into cloud bets and raced up the chart. Alibaba built regional dominance in Asia. And Oracle — once a database titan — struggled to translate legacy software cash into cloud growth and ultimately flattened while rivals soared.

In this visualization you’ll see launch years, COVID acceleration (2020), the AI/compute demand surge (2022–2025), and a dramatic split where one legacy giant is left behind. Data shown are provider cloud revenues (billions USD) by year; years with no business are plotted as $0. Sources include company financial disclosures, earnings releases, and industry reports.

Like, subscribe, and hit the bell if you want a breakdown episode (deep dive on numbers & sources). Drop a comment: which cloud will dominate AI compute by 2030?
